ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Forecasting Capabilities of General-Purpose LLMs on Scientific Time Series
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of a popular LLM (e.g. T5, BART) on a diverse set of scientific time series forecasting tasks (e.g. gravitational wave detection, astronomical light curve classification, weather forecasting) using real-world benchmarks. This baseline will be extended to include a range of models specifically designed for time series forecasting (e.g. Prophet, ARIMA) and attention-based LLM variants.
CONTROLS: Baseline performance of general-purpose LLMs; performance of models specifically designed for time series forecasting; comparison of LLM variants that incorporate time series-specific architectures.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This study will demonstrate that while LLMs are strong overall, specialized models for time series forecasting are still superior for specific tasks; however, suitable adaptation and specialization can improve LLM performance in these tasks. 

Domains:  gravitational wave detection, astronomical light curve classification, weather forecasting

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Study of Texture and Visualisation Methods for Scientific Time Series Representation
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the suitability of texture and visualization methods for representation of scientific time series data, focusing on effectiveness for downstream LLM tasks (e.g. classification, regression, generation). This will involve comparing image-based representations of time series from various disciplines (e.g. gravitational waveforms, seismic signals, bioacoustic recordings) using widely used visualisation tools (e.g. CNNs, autoencoders).
CONTROLS: Text-based representation methods (e.g. array-to-string conversion, sequence formatting); comparison of different visualisation tools and architectures.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This study will reveal that texture and visualisation methods fail to adequately represent complex patterns and relationships in scientific time series data, resulting in disappointing performance on certain LLM tasks. However, it may also identify specific cases or domains where these methods can offer better insights.

Domains: gravitational wave detection, bioacoustics, EEG analysis and ECG analysis.

TITLE: Investigating the Optimization Strategies of LLMs for Scientific Time Series
REVISE: 1
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of various optimization strategies on the performance of LLMs for scientific time series tasks, including warm-starting from pre-trained models, incorporating tasks into meta-learning frameworks, and adapting the model architecture specifically for time-series data. This should involve experiments on multiple real-world datasets from diverse disciplines (e.g., gravitational wave detection, astronomical light curves, ECG analysis).
CONTROLS: Baseline LLM performance with random initialization; meta-learning frameworks adapted for time series data without pre-training; incorporating specific domain knowledge into the model architecture.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Optimizing LLMs with adapted architectures and warm-starting with pre-trained models will prove crucial for tapping their full potential in times series tasks, with significant improvements in performance on a variety of disciplines. However, hyperparameter tuning may require substantial manual effort due to the model's sensitivity.

Domains: gravitational wave detection, astronomical light curves, ECG analysis, bioacoustics

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hypernym-based Neural-Symbolic Reasoning Framework for Explaining Scientific Time Series
PROPOSAL: Design and implement a new neural-symbolic framework centered around hypernymy for explaining scientific time series data. This approach allows combining symbolic reasoning with neural networks, and aims to identify gaps in the generalisation of LLMs to various domains. We investigate how leveraging symbolic domain knowledge allows a general-purpose LLM to better comprehend the underlying complex structures in a range of time series tasks.
CONTROLS: Comparison of the proposed neural-symbolic framework against commonly employed LLMs for time series data, without the use of domain-specific information.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The integrated symbolic knowledge system is expected to outperform LLMs in explaining complex systems for a wide range of scientific time series, with several applications in physics, biology, and meteorology.

Domains: chaotic system forecasting, astronomical light curve classification, physical system dynamics

TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Temporal Feature Engineering on LLMs for Scientific Time Series
PROPOSAL: Examine the effect of incorporating time-domainExtractor representations, which allowed a time series model to capture meaningful temporal features (e.g., frequency, periodicity), into existing LLM architectures for various scientific time series tasks. Our aim is to investigate if pre-trained features lead to a unified time series representation that withstands domain boundaries.
CONTROLS: LLM performance when taking in raw time series data versus time-domainExtractor-based representations.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The study will reveal that applying time-domainExtractor features to LLMs promotes robust domain understanding, boosting generalisation across distinct scientific time series tasks and sustaining impressive performance even in unforeseen domains.

Domains: astronomical light curves, BCIs (Brain-Computer Interface) data, seismology

TITLE: Towards Adaptive Sampling for Scientific Time Series LLMs
PROPOSAL: Propose an adaptive sampling strategy for downsampling high-resolution scientific time series to compress data without affecting the model's performance, thereby mitigating the high computational demands associated with LLMs handling these datasets. Evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed sampling strategy on several high-resolution time series datasets from diverse scientific disciplines (e.g., gravitational wave detection, astronomical light curves, electrical signals).
CONTROLS: Investigation of pre-defined sampling strategies, such as uniform sampling and random sampling, in comparison with the proposed adaptive method.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect a notable reduction in computation time while preserving model accuracy, making the approach suitable for use in high-dimensional and high-resolution LLM-based time series tasks across various scientific fields.

Domains: gravitational wave detection, astronomy

TITLE: Evaluating Text-Only Transformers for Scientific Time Series Classification
PROPOSAL: Investigate the performance of popular text-only transformer models, such as BERT and RoBERTa, on a wide range of scientific time series classification tasks across various domains (e.g., gravitational wave detection, astronomical light curve classification, seismology, bioacoustics, EEG analysis) using real-world benchmarks and datasets.

TITLE: Investigating Multimodal LLMs for Scientific Time Series Understanding and Generation
PROPOSAL: Explore the effectiveness of popular multimodal LLMs, such as CLIP, DALL-E, and BlenderBot, in understanding and generating scientific time series data across various domains (e.g., EEG analysis, ECG analysis, human activity recognition) using a combination of text and image representations of signals.

However, they might fail to generalize well to smaller datasets or image representations that are not specifically tailored for time series data.

- UKDaEDF 
- OpenHuman activity recognition

TITLE: Specialized Temporal Embeddings for Scientific Time Series
PROPOSAL: Investigate the design and effectiveness of specialized temporal embeddings for scientific time series, which are tailored to capture the unique characteristics and patterns of time series data in various domains (e.g., gravitational wave detection, astronomical light curve classification, seismology). Specifically, we will explore the use of periodic, exponential, and logarithmic functions to represent temporal patterns, and compare their performance against general-purpose temporal embeddings.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of specialized temporal embeddings against general-purpose ones, ablate the impact of different temporal embedding functions, and control for dataset size and sequence length.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that specialized temporal embeddings will outperform general-purpose ones in understanding and generation tasks, especially in domains where temporal patterns are critical. However, the models might require additional tuning to handle variations in temporal patterns across different domains.

Evaluation metrics: IG index, ROCAUC, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR)

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Extending Multimodal LLMs to Unified Time Series Modelling
PROPOSAL: Explore the extension of multimodal LLMs to unified time series modelling, which enables the simultaneous understanding and generation of heterogeneous scientific time series data across various domains (e.g., gravitational wave detection, astronomical light curve classification, seismology). Specifically, we will design a joint embedding module that learns to capture the shared and distinct features of different time series modalities, and demonstrate its effectiveness on a range of scientific time series tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of unified multimodal LLMs against specialized temporal embeddings and general-purpose multimodal LLMs, ablate the impact of different joint embedding architectures, and control for dataset size and sequence length.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that unified multimodal LLMs will provide a significant improvement over specialized temporal embeddings and general-purpose multimodal LLMs in understanding and generation tasks, especially in domains where time series heterogeneity is high. However, the models might require additional computational resources and dataset corrections for scaling up their analysis.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing the Robustness of Large Language Models to Time Series Noise
PROPOSAL: Investigate the robustness of large language models (LLMs) to noise and inaccuracies in time series data, which is a critical aspect of scientific time series applications. Specifically, we will generate noisy versions of scientific time series datasets and evaluate the performance of LLMs on these noisy datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of LLMs on noisy datasets against their performance on clean datasets, ablate the impact of different noise types and levels, and control for dataset size and sequence length.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that LLMs will be sensitive to noise and inaccuracies in time series data, and that their performance will degrade significantly on noisy datasets. However, we also anticipate that LLMs will be more robust to certain types of noise, such as random noise or missing values, than others, such as cyclostationary noise or abrupt changes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Addressing the Challenge of Temporal Shift Invariance in LLMs
PROPOSAL: Investigate the challenge of temporal shift invariance in large language models (LLMs), which arises when the order of time steps in a time series sequence is altered, but the underlying dynamics remain the same. We will evaluate the performance of LLMs on shifted versions of scientific time series data and propose techniques to address this challenge, such as a novel temporal shift invariant architecture or a data augmentation strategy.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of LLMs with and without the proposed techniques, ablate the impact of different shifting schemes, and control for dataset size and sequence length.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that LLMs will be sensitive to temporal shifts in input data and that addressing this challenge will be crucial for their successful application in scientific time series analysis. By developing techniques to handle temporal shift invariance, we anticipate significant improvements in the robustness and accuracy of LLMs on time series tasks.
